Talk on technicalities dominate 1st House hearing on system loss abolition. House members sought clarification on the highly technical nature of system loss on Wednesday, Aug. 6 as the Committee on Energy held its first hearing to discuss issues and concerns surrounding the proposed abolition of system loss charges from electricity bills. Pangasinan 2nd district Rep. Mark Cojuangco was among the solons in the hearing who espoused an objective take on the issue to avoid further misconceptions on how technical losses occur in power distribution systems. The hearing was held in response to President Marcos' call to scrap systems loss charges, which he articulated in his July 27 State of the Nation Address (SONA) to a standing ovation. Cojuangco, chairman of the Committee on Nuclear Energy, acknowledged that energy losses were inherent in any system and cautioned against portraying all system loss as inefficiency. He likened the issue to the thermal efficiency of an internal combustion engine. According to him, only around 30 percent of the energy in fuel is converted into useful work, while the rest is dissipated as heat. “Ibig sabihin, 70 percent ng energy ng gasolina ay natatapon bilang init ng makina, exhaust, etc. Ibig sabihin ba nitong system loss na reklamo natin ay bawal maningil ang taxi driver ng kabuuan ng kanyang gasolina niya dahil 70 percent ay natapon sa system loss? It doesn't make sense," he said. (It means 70 percent of the energy from gasoline is wasted as engine heat, exhaust, etc. Does this mean that the system loss we complain about would prevent a taxi driver from charging for all his gasoline since 70 percent is wasted in system loss? It doesn’t make sense.) "I hope we can soul-search and look at this dispassionately because we might be misleading our people,” said the veteran lawmaker. The discussion came as lawmakers examined the factors contributing to technical system losses. Cojuangco further said the public should look at the theoretical maximum efficiency of a distribution utility (DU) versus the actual efficiency level of private DUs and electric cooperatives to show if “the DU is truly doing its best to reduce technical system losses." What about electric cooperatives? Meanwhile, Deputy Minority Leader and APEC Partylist Rep. Sergio Dagooc echoed that discussions on system loss should also take into account the distinct regulatory framework governing electric cooperatives. He said that electric cooperatives are non-stock, non-profit entities owned by their member-consumers, unlike private DUs that are investor-owned. Dagooc--a member of the so-called House Power Bloc--warned that removing the system loss charge could have a disproportionate impact on electric cooperatives, which may not have the financial capacity to absorb the cost. He noted that under the Energy Regulatory Commission's (ERC) cash flow methodology, the objective was neither for electric cooperatives to earn profits nor incur losses but to cover the cost of serving the people. These include personnel expenses and network maintenance. "If system loss is removed without corresponding adjustments, the funds intended for salaries and maintenance will instead be used to absorb those costs," Dagooc said. ERC Chaiperson Nino Juan agreed that electric cooperatives could face cash flow constraints because their current rates do not include any allowance for absorbing system loss costs. He added that that unless rates are reset to provide additional operating funds, cooperatives may struggle to sustain operations while working to reduce non-technical losses. Dagooc further clarified that “[DUs] do not earn from systems loss,” which Juan confirmed. Illustrating the point, the lawmaker explained that if a generator delivers 100 kilowatt-hours but only 90 kilowatt-hours (kWh) are registered at consumers' meters, the remaining 10 kWh constitute system loss. Since generators bill DUs for the full 100 kWh delivered, existing laws – particularly Republic Act (RA) No. 7832 and the Electric Power Industry Reform Act of 2001 (EPIRA), allow utilities to recover allowable system loss costs from consumers. “Kaya pinapayagan ng batas, RA No. 7832, at sinalo sa Section 43f ng EPIRA, na ipasa kasi hindi pumapayag yang generator na 90 lang ang babayaran ko. Ang sinisingil ay 100. Kaya ultimately, yung siningil ko na sa systems loss na sampung kilowatt hour may bayad din,” Dagooc said. TL vs. NTL Committee on Energy Chairman and Palawan 2nd district Rep. Jose Alvarez distinguished between technical system (TL) loss and non-technical systems loss (NTL) during the hearing. For him, charges arising from the latter can be easily removed. “Yung NTL po ay pwede tanggalin kaagad, ngunit yung TL ay gawan ng paraan kung papaano ma-minimize pa talaga, hindi man outright [removal],” Alvarez said. (The NTL can be removed immediately, but the TL should be addressed in a way that it can really be minimized, even if not outright removed.) NTL is electricity theft and pilferage that leads to operational and administrative loss while TL is the electricity transmission lost through the network. Cagayan de Oro City Rep. Rufus Rodriguez on the other hand said Congress cannot outrightly abolish system loss, technical or otherwise, and suggested further studies into the matter. "You cannot remove everything…but indeed, we can lower [the TL],” Rodriguez said. Bagong Henerasyon (BH) Party-list Rep. Robert Nazal maintained that honest consumers should not be treated as shock absorbers of NTLs, inefficiencies, defective systems, and failure of electricity utilities to improve. “Hanggang kailan pagbabayarin ang taong bayan para sa losses na dapat responsibilidad ng utilities na bawasan?” Nazal asked. (Until when will the people be made to pay for losses that should be the responsibility of utilities to reduce?)

Winna Go’s ‘Seams of Memory’ book launches at M Museum. In “Seams of Memory,” Winna Go shows us the artist's heartfelt journey to hone her talent over the years. Now, it's forever immortalized as a hardbound book. As guests enter the Metropolitan Museum of Metro Manila, the first thing they’ll likely notice by the lobby entrance is the inviting canvas that is the “Circle of Vitality.” Its square pieces feel like a quilt that is made up of fragments from all of Winna’s works on display. Once it draws you inside, you see the very pieces that helped bring the centerpiece to life. At first glance, it may seem like similar Chinese dresses replicated over the years, but as you take a closer look, you’ll prove this assumption wrong. Every fold and pattern on the dresses paints a different story. With “Vessel of Abundance,” we see just how seamlessly she forms these patterns on the dresses. It almost feels lifelike and ready to be worn. Meanwhile, “Embroidered Thoughts” grants us this window into the eyes of the artist. It lets us see the dresses that act as the exhibit’s unifying theme and how looming family photos and heirlooms paint a picture of her heritage. From her book, titled after the exhibit, this process is explored even further. It showcases Winna’s work and accompanies it with a style of Chinese poetry known as jueju. If viewing the works at the gallery was enough to awaken something within you, don't hesitate to grab your own copy to let her works linger long after the exhibit's run ends. Winna Go’s “Seams of Memory” is currently on an extended run at the M Museum until Aug. 16, 2026. Copies of her book can be purchased at the Met Museum and the Art Cube Gallery.

QC bags 31st Apolinario Mabini Award for PWD inclusion. The Quezon City government has been named the Local Government Unit Awardee (City Category) at the 31st Apolinario Mabini Awards in recognition of its sustained efforts to promote the welfare, inclusion, and equal opportunities of persons with disabilities (PWDs). Mayor Joy Belmonte received the award during the Aug. 3 ceremony at the Romualdez Hall of the House of Representatives, where the Philippine Foundation for the Rehabilitation of the Disabled, Inc. (PFRD) honored local government units and institutions for their outstanding contributions to advancing the rights and inclusion of PWDs. Following the awarding ceremony, Quezon City Persons with Disability Affairs Office head Debbie Dacanay formally presented the award to Belmonte on behalf of the city government. The recognition highlights Quezon City's continuing implementation of programs that promote an inclusive, accessible, and caring community through its Persons with Disability Affairs Office. Belmonte said the award affirms the city government's commitment to building "a more inclusive, accessible, and caring city for all." Speaking before awardees, government officials, and PWD advocates, House Speaker Faustino "Bojie" G. Dy III thanked the PFRD for holding the 31st Apolinario Mabini Awards at the House of Representatives, saying it was an honor for the chamber to host a ceremony recognizing individuals and institutions that demonstrate an inclusive Philippines is possible. Pujalte stands by review of P3.225-B TB procurement amid Ombudsman complaint. Amid a complaint filed against him before the Office of the Ombudsman, Department of Health (DOH) Secretary Jose “Brix” Pujalte Jr. said on Thursday, Aug. 6, that the department's review of the proposed P3-billion procurement of tuberculosis commodities is intended to protect patients and ensure the proper use of public funds. On Aug. 5, health advocates asked the OMB to impose a preventive suspension on Pujalte and initiate a graft case before the Sandiganbayan over the alleged irregular suspension of the procurement of P3.225 billion worth of tuberculosis drugs. “Wala pa tayong 30 days sa posisyon, pero gusto agad pabilisin ang pag-apruba sa P3 billion na TB procurement nang walang malalimang pagsusuri (We’ve been in the position for less than 30 days, yet there is already pressure to fast-track the approval of the ₱3-billion tuberculosis procurement without a thorough review),” Pujalte said in a statement. He stressed that the proposed P3-billion procurement involves taxpayers’ money and warrants careful scrutiny, saying the government should have learned from the Pharmally case as the lives of patients are at stake. “Three billion pesos po ’yan ng taumbayan, hindi ’yan basta-basta. Natuto na dapat tayo sa nangyari noon sa Pharmally. Buhay ng tao ang nakataya rito (That is P3 billion belonging to the people. It is not something to be treated lightly. We should have learned from what happened with Pharmally. Human lives are at stake here),” he said. According to Pujalte, he respects the authority and procedures of the Office of the Ombudsman and stands ready to provide all relevant documents and records it may require for its investigation. The DOH chief said he would not be distracted by what he called a continuing demolition campaign and would instead remain committed to safeguarding public funds and the welfare of Filipinos. “Kahit sunod-sunod ang demolition job, hindi tayo magpapa-distract. Ang pera ng bayan at buhay ng Pilipino, kailangang protektahan (Despite the successive demolition job, we will not be distracted. Public funds and the lives of Filipinos must be protected),” he said. Earlier, Pujalte denied claims that he had been gambling at a casino. He then explained that he had gone to a restaurant in a hotel complex for a courtesy call with local government mayors. President Marcos appointed Pujalte as DOH secretary on July 13 following the resignation of Dr. Teodoro Herbosa.

Nearly 7,000 people taking shelter in evacuation centers amid severe weather. The severe weather that has affected parts of the country has forced thousands of people from their homes, with nearly 7,000 now taking shelter in evacuation centers, the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) said on Thursday, Aug. 6. In its latest disaster response report, DSWD said 2,219 families, or 6,893 individuals, are staying in 35 evacuation centers in Ilocos Region, Central Luzon, and Zamboanga Peninsula. Another 426 families, or 1,419 individuals, are temporarily staying with relatives or friends, bringing the total number of displaced persons to 8,312 in the Cordillera Administrative Region (CAR), Ilocos Region, Central Luzon, and Zamboanga Peninsula. DSWD said the effects of the enhanced southwest monsoon (habagat), and recently, Tropical Depression Luis and Tropical Storm Maymay, have affected 26,412 families, or 88,738 individuals, in 290 barangays across CAR, Ilocos Region, Cagayan Valley, Central Luzon, Bicol Region, and Zamboanga Peninsula. It also reported that 13 houses were damaged, including one that was totally destroyed and 12 that sustained partial damage in CAR, Ilocos Region, and Cagayan Valley. DSWD has so far provided ₱1,998,384.25 worth of humanitarian assistance to affected families. Of the total, ₱1,798,072.78 came from the DSWD, while ₱200,311.47 was extended by local government units. DSWD said it continues to keep relief resources on standby, including ₱1.58 billion in quick response fund, more than five million family food packs, and ₱1.33 billion worth of other food and non food items for immediate deployment.

WHO chief says Ebola outbreak is outpacing response as aid workers strike over pay. KINSHASA, Congo (AP) — The world’s fastest-growing Ebola outbreak is spreading faster than efforts to fight it, the head of the World Health Organization said on Wednesday during a visit to Congo where some health workers are striking over a lack of pay. Nearly three months into the outbreak, new cases are doubling in some hot spots, Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said in a post on X after meeting with officials in the capital, Kinshasa. It was the second visit by the WHO director-general to the Central African country since the outbreak was declared in mid-May. “We all agree that we must urgently and massively scale up all our efforts across all pillars of the response and by all partners,” Tedros said. The outbreak has accounted for 3,874 confirmed cases, including 1,751 deaths, as of Monday, according to the latest data from Congo’s Ministry of Health. In Ituri province, the epicenter of the outbreak, families said many front line workers have gone on strike, worsening access to healthcare that was already challenged by rebel conflict in one of Congo's most remote and vulnerable areas, its east near the borders of South Sudan, Uganda and Rwanda. While some workers say they have started receiving payment in the last week for work done since the outbreak began, they are demanding improved wages. Anicet Baluku, a resident of Bunia, the capital of Itur, blamed the death of his two brothers from Ebola on the strike. “We urge the authorities to quickly find a solution to prevent other families from experiencing the same tragedy,” he told The Associated Press. The U.S. Department of State said on Wednesday that it will provide an additional $242 million in funding for immediate Ebola response and preparedness efforts in the region and for humanitarian assistance related to the outbreak. Such funding, it said in a statement, has now exceeded $512 million in direct assistance. The outbreak has eclipsed all previous Ebola outbreaks in its speed of transmission and is the second-largest outbreak on record, behind the 2014-2016 West Africa outbreak that recorded more than 28,000 cases, including over 11,000 deaths. The Bundibugyo virus that is causing this outbreak has no approved treatment or vaccine, and local officials believe it began in a remote area long before it was declared on May 15. The outbreak is still “spreading at an alarming and unprecedented rate,” the medical charity Doctors Without Borders said on Wednesday, adding: “The response is expanding but is still not reaching communities quickly enough to break transmission chains.” Dr. Jean Kaseya, head of the Africa Centers for Disease and Control, said on Tuesday during a visit to Bunia that contact tracing isn't working, with at least 60% to 70% of new cases coming outside of those being monitored after exposure to patients. Late detection of cases has been a key contributor to the 45% fatality rate, officials say. Of the 77 most-recent cases reported during a 24-hour period, 44 were fatal, according to the health ministry. At least 717 patients are in isolation while 749 patients have recovered. Kaseya, who met with Tedros on Wednesday, said Africa CDC is aligning its efforts with responders “around earlier detection, stronger contact tracing, rapid access to quality care and deeper engagement with communities.” Tedros called for action to reach all affected localities, strengthen coordination under the government’s leadership and protect health workers. “Above all, communities must be at the center of and have ownership of the response,” he said. “We cannot stop Ebola without their trust, leadership and partnership.”

Pang-Guinness? Cops arrest all 10 most wanted fugitives in Western Visayas in just 4 days. Police arrested all the top 10 fugitives in Western Visayas in just four days after the regional most wanted list was updated for the month of August this year—one of the fastest, if not the fastest, accounting of top level wanted persons recorded so far in the Philippine National Police (PNP). The complete sweep of the 10 most wanted in the region for this month was the third time the Police Regional Office 6 recorded it, the first was accomplished in June this year for eight days, followed by the 14-day operations that arrested all the wanted operations for the month of July. PRO 6 Brig. Gen. Randulf T. Tuaño attributed the three consecutive sweeps of Western Visayas’ most wanted to intelligence-driven manhunt operations. “Three complete sweeps of the Regional Top 10 most wanted persons list are not the result of chance—they are the product of disciplined intelligence work, seamless coordination, and the unwavering commitment of our officers,” said Tuaño. “This accomplishment is not about numbers alone; it is about ensuring that those accused of serious crimes are brought before our courts and that our communities are safer because justice is actively pursued,” he added. The arrested fugitives were facing serious criminal charges, including murder, rape, acts of lasciviousness, sexual assault, and other offenses. Tuaño said the operations were carried out through intensified intelligence gathering, surveillance, target profiling, warrant service, and close coordination among operating units, intelligence personnel, investigators, and partner law enforcement agencies. PNP chief Gen. Jose Melencio C. Nartatez, Jr., earlier tasked all territorial police commanders, from regional down to the station level, to intensify the campaign against wanted persons. He said the aggressive campaign against wanted fugitives since in most cases, the wanted persons are usually involved in two or more criminal activities. Nartatez particularly tasked police commanders to regularly update their respective most wanted list, citing several accomplishments where some police units would account for all the 10 most wanted persons. Tuaño, for his part, said that while the regional top 10 list has been fully accounted for, their campaign against wanted persons remains far from over. “Our police units throughout Western Visayas will continue intensifying intelligence collection, warrant service, and focused manhunt operations to locate other fugitives and ensure they are brought before the courts without delay,” he said.

Can Killa Kush x Ferca Beauty help you create the perfect lip combo?. With endless makeup tutorials, viral hacks, and ever-changing beauty trends filling social media feeds, creating the perfect look can sometimes feel overwhelming. But amid all the noise, one beauty essential continues to stand the test of time: a good lip combo. Whether it's a subtle nude or a bold statement shade, the right combination of lip products has the power to instantly brighten a mood and elevate an entire look. It is no surprise that beauty brands continue to reinvent lip products, offering new formulas and finishes that cater to different styles and preferences. The latest to join the growing lineup is local makeup brand Ferca Beauty, which has teamed up with content creator Killa Kush for the launch of the WTFerc Collection. Designed around the idea that a simple lip transformation can make a big difference, the collection features two products that can be mixed and matched to create personalized lip combinations. Leading the lineup is the WTF!? Lip Marker, a long-wearing lip marker formulated with mark and lock technology making it lightweight with transfer-resistant color. Available in the six shades with brown undertone, it can be used to define, overline, shade, or completely fill the lips for long-lasting wear. But beyond lips, we found it also perfect as eyeliners even for those with sensitive eyes. The color it has can instantly elevate your eye makeup for those captivating eyes. Complementing it is the WTF!? Lip Plumper, a high-shine lip treatment formulated with pillowplump complex to help lips appear fuller while the cushion moisture blend delivers hydration. Available in six shades, the gloss provides a cooling sensation while helping lips look smoother, plumper, and more voluminous. What we love about it is that even though it is positioned as a limp plumper, it is not spicy unlike other plumpers that feel like burning your lips. For Killa, the collaboration reflects the evolution of her personal style rather than following complicated beauty routines. "I never really considered myself a beauty guru. I've always just known what I like and what works for me," she told Manila Bulletin Lifestyle. "My routine has always been pretty simple too, but my style has evolved over the years. That's what I love about this collection. It shows how something as small as changing up your lip combo can really transform your look." She hopes the collection gives users the same confidence she associates with finding the perfect lip combination. "When people try the collection, they will feel like that girl," she said. "There's just something about a good lip combo that gives you a little boost. Some people invest in a great pair of heels or a designer bag to feel their best, but I truly think the right lip can do the same." Beyond launching another influencer collaboration, Killa believes authenticity is what ultimately determines whether a beauty collection resonates with consumers. "I think the products always have to speak for themselves," she said. "No matter how big the influencer is or how extravagant the launch is, people won't engage if the product isn't genuinely good and if they feel like the influencer wouldn't even use it." She added that the collaboration came from a long-held dream and intentionally focused on simplicity. "I knew exactly what I wanted: two products with six shades each that people could mix and match to create their own perfect lip combo. It felt authentic to me, and I think that's what matters most."

Eala-mania takes over Toronto as Filipina star draws another packed crowd. The Alex Eala frenzy has reached the National Bank Open in Toronto, Canada with thousands of fans packing Sobeys Stadium to cheer on the Filipina star in her second-round showdown against Alycia Parks on Thursday, Aug. 6 (Philippine time). Eala rewarded the crowd with another gritty performance, outlasting Parks, 6-1, 4-6, 6-3, to advance to the third round. Beyond the win, the 21-year-old rising star expressed her gratitude for the overwhelming support as fans filled the stands and created a lively atmosphere throughout the match. “I just came off from Washington and I just feel like this is a celebration,” said Eala, referring to her breakthrough WTA Tour title win at the Mubadala DC Open. “Linggo-lingo ko kayong nakikita, sinusuporta ako. Linggo-linggo kong nakikita kung gaano nyo kamahal ang kapwa nyong Pinoy kaya proud na proud akong maging Pinoy. Salamat, mga kababayan,” she added. Eala also acknowledged that the overwhelming support she has been receiving extends beyond her own journey, shining a brighter spotlight on tennis as a sport. “Thank you to everyone who’s here supporting tennis and creating atmospheres like this. It’s really the pleasure of my life to experience these things,” said Eala. With the support of fans behind her, Eala moves into the next round brimming with confidence and momentum as she continues her pursuit of another WTA Tour crown -- this time, on an even bigger stage.

Digital Cities and IT-BMP sector are reshaping commercial real estate. For 2028, the Information Technology and Business Process Management (IT-BPM) sector is expected to continue expanding steadily, with projections suggesting revenue targets between $43.3 billion and $50.5 billion annually, and the workforce could reach around 2.14 million employees, according to the IT and Business Process Association of the Philippines. The IT-BPM sector continues to play a significant role in the Philippine economy, contributing an estimated 8 percent of the national GDP. Even as global outsourcing evolves, the country continues to benefit from its reputation for service quality, strong communication skills, and cultural compatibility with Western markets. As one of the country’s leading economic contributors, the BPO and IT-BPM sectors generate significant employment opportunities and stimulate the real estate sector by driving demand for office space requirements. The sector’s expansion is aligned to the Digital Cities program, a strategic initiative by the Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT) to decentralize economic growth by transforming countryside locations into thriving hubs for the Information Technology and Business Process Management (IT-BPM) industry. In its 2025 list, the DICT identified 25 high-growth locations nationwide that ranked highly on a four-point evaluation system that included factors such as talent availability, infrastructure, cost-effectiveness, and business environment. The program adds cities through periodic recognition cycles beyond the original list established in 2020, backed by a longer-term government roadmap through 2028. In its mid-year property market outlook, Lobien Realty Group reported that “active BPO and IT-BMP demand is moving toward DICT-designated Digital Cities. These emerging municipalities offer competitive setups, tax incentives, and highly capable provincial talent pools.” For Shiela Lobien, CEO of Lobien Realty Group, the movement towards Digital Cities signals a structural change. “Metro Manila and leading digital cities are moving in opposite directions. The capital region’s vacancy rate remains elevated, having risen sharply during the POGO fallout, though prime districts like Makati and BGC have remained comparatively resilient, while secondary submarkets lag. In contrast, several digital cities are seeing vacancy tighten, shifting leverage towards landlords in those markets.” Several events proved to be catalysts for the shift to Digital Cities among IT-BPM companies, as cited by Lobien. “The pandemic proved service delivery doesn't require a single centralized office, weakening the case for Metro Manila concentration. The 2024 POGO shutdown then removed a significant volume of office demand almost overnight, pushing Metro Manila vacancy to one of its highest levels in decades. Add ongoing macroeconomic uncertainty and caution from global clients following the Iran conflict, and companies are now prioritizing cost stability and lower risk exposure.” In Digital Cities, IT-BPM companies can benefit from lower operating costs, local talent pools, and business support. Lobien added that there is no POGO-related oversupply and that legal support under CREATE MORE formally permits hybrid and work-from-home arrangements while preserving tax incentives. To capitalize on the shift, Lobien encourages developers to prioritize incentive-registered office space, alongside hybrid-ready, flexible floor plates and residential components that capture housing demand as jobs grow in the region. “Investors can benefit from lower entry costs and tightening vacancy versus a Metro Manila market still absorbing the POGO shock, with government backing reducing (not eliminating) risk. Shared services and global capability centers are a high-growth segment worth early positioning. At the same time, buyers can leverage affordability arbitrage, prices and rents well below Metro Manila, with values historically appreciating once local employment scales,” Lobien said. Since the sector has lowered its own 2028 growth targets and corporate decisions have slowed considerably due to AI disruption, rising global competition, and geopolitical uncertainty, Lobien also cautioned buyers to take discipline in city selection and timelines seriously. Given these circumstances, Lobien remains optimistic about Digital Cities' upward trajectory. “Continued pressure on Metro Manila, from pandemic-driven shifts, the POGO exit, and cautious global clients amid macro- and geopolitical uncertainty, reinforces the case for expanding recognized alternatives. However, growth will not be evenly distributed. With the industry's own long-term targets revised downward due to AI adoption and rising competition, capital and hiring will likely concentrate in proven performers rather than spread quickly across new entrants. Expect the Digital Cities list to broaden in name faster than in actual investment, at least in the near term.”

DA-BPI, Mitsui partner on mango crop protection research. The Department of Agriculture–Bureau of Plant Industry (DA-BPI) and Mitsui & Co. (Asia Pacific) Pte. Ltd. Manila Branch signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) on July 29, 2026, to launch a research collaboration on an innovative crop protection technology for the Philippine mango industry. The signing was led by BPI Director Gerald Glenn F. Panganiban, Ph.D., and Mitsui Manila General Manager Marilen R. Francisco, and witnessed by Agriculture Secretary Francisco P. Tiu Laurel Jr., Undersecretary-Designate for Identified High-Value Export Crops and Agri-Fishery Export Development and Promotion Philip C. Young, Mitsui & Co.'s Chief Strategy Officer of the Asia-Pacific Business Unit Takanubu Murayama and Deputy Branch General Manager Lysander Quinones. Under the MOU, both parties will undertake pre-trial research on a controlled-release crop protection technology designed to improve the effectiveness of crop protection applications while reducing resistance development, runoff, and ultraviolet degradation. The collaboration will generate technical and regulatory data, including residue and dosage studies, to support the future evaluation and registration of the technology in the Philippines. Through this partnership, DA-BPI will provide technical guidance, coordinate pre-trial activities, identify suitable mango trial sites, and work closely with mango growers and other stakeholders. The initiative supports the development of science-based solutions to address key production challenges, including cecid fly infestation, and reinforces DA-BPI's commitment to strengthening the competitiveness and sustainability of the Philippine mango industry.

Century Pacific overcomes GenSan quake impact to post higher profit. Po-led Century Pacific Food Inc. (CNPF) reported a six-percent growth in net income to ₱4.1 billion for the first half of 2026 from ₱3.9 billion in the same period last year, as higher margins offset higher expenses, finance costs, and the impact of earthquake damage. In a disclosure to the Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE) on Thursday, Aug. 6, CNPF said its gross margin stood at 25.9 percent, expanding by 20 basis points (bps) from the same period last year. This offset the 20-bp increase in operating expenses (opex) as a percentage of sales, leading operating income to increase by 15 percent versus the same period last year, in lockstep with topline growth. During the period, the company saw an increase in finance costs and its effective tax rate due to a moderate uptick in short-term debt and the expiration of tax incentives. CNPF recognized one-off items during the period resulting from the impact of the earthquake that hit General Santos City, where key manufacturing hubs are located, in June. Excluding the impact of the earthquake, core operating income growth registered at 18 percent in the first half of 2026, while core net income after tax grew by 10 percent year-on-year. These non-recurring provisions for damaged inventory and facilities are still subject to insurance claims, with timing differences in recognition. Amid an increasingly volatile environment, CNPF was able to sustain its growth momentum, delivering a 15-percent growth in consolidated revenues to ₱45.8 billion. The firm said its dual-engine portfolio—branded and original equipment manufacturer (OEM) exports—grew by double digits on both fronts. A majority of CNPF’s sales come from its predominantly domestic branded business, comprising marine, meat, milk, coconut, and other emerging segments. Despite a soft consumer landscape, the branded business remained resilient, supported by the relevance of its diverse portfolio of affordable staples. During the second quarter, the segment accelerated, increasing by 14 percent versus the same period last year and lifting first-half growth to 13 percent. Sales improvements were seen across all branded subsegments, with the milk, coconut, and other emerging businesses leading the charge. OEM tuna and coconut exports continued their recovery from a challenging first half of 2025. In the first half of this year, the segment grew 26 percent year-on-year on the back of improving tuna export markets and robust global demand for healthy coconut products. However, the segment’s second-quarter performance was dampened by the June earthquake that hit General Santos, where key manufacturing facilities are located, resulting in a 21-percent year-on-year growth. “Our operating conditions in the first half were far from smooth. Fuel prices soared, squeezing our consumers while adding pressure to our operating costs,” said CNPF Chief Financial Officer (CFO) Richard S. Manapat. He explained, “Against this backdrop, cost discipline became all the more important. We proactively tightened spending while also rolling out measured pricing action well below inflation, aiming to strike a balance between cushioning rising costs and keeping our goods within reach for our consumers.” “At Century Pacific, the aspiration to sustain our momentum in the double-digit growth territory remains. As headwinds persist, we are focused on navigating the year as smoothly as possible, while remaining steadfast in pursuing long-term growth opportunities,” Manapat added. CNPF’s near-term priorities include shoring up inventory for food security and business continuity, keeping a tight rein on spending, and strengthening its value-for-money offerings for consumers. At the same time, investment in capacity expansion continues across all of the company’s businesses. CNPF has earmarked approximately ₱8 billion for capital expenditure (capex) this year, double its typical annual investment, reflecting confidence in the company’s growth prospects. - James A. Loyola

PRO-13 nets 680 loose firearms in 8 months. BUTUAN CITY – A total of 416 law enforcement operations against loose firearms were conducted by the stations and units of the Police Regional Office (PRO) in the Caraga region from January to August this year. ‎ During the period, 133 individuals were arrested, and 680 loose firearms were either confiscated, surrendered, or deposited. ‎ "The intensified campaign against loose firearms is among the priorities of PRO-13 (Caraga) Director Police Brig. Gen. Marcial Mariano Magistrado IV to ensure the safety of residents in the region," PRO-13 information chief Police Lt. Col. Jennifer Ometer said in an interview on Thursday. ‎ Data provided by the regional police indicated that of the 416 operations during the period, 11 were conducted by the Agusan del Norte Police, 209 by the Agusan del Sur Police, 85 by the Surigao del Norte Police, 21 by the Surigao del Sur Police, 20 by the Dinagat Islands Police, 33 by the Butuan City Police, and 37 by the Regional Mobile Force Battalion (RMFB). ‎ A total of 19 individuals were arrested in Agusan del Norte, 21 in Agusan del Sur, five in Surigao del Norte, 29 in Surigao del Sur, one in Dinagat Islands, 22 in Butuan City, and 36 by the RMFB. ‎ The highest number of firearms was confiscated in Agusan del Sur with 225, followed by Surigao del Sur with 143, Agusan del Norte with 117, Surigao del Norte with 91, Butuan City with 48, RMFB with 36, and Dinagat Islands with 20. ‎ "The campaign against loose firearms is also aimed to deter lawless elements from utilizing loose firearms in criminal activities in the region," Ometer said.
